The test image shows a tomato stem at the soil line, cut open longitudinally. Key features:
- White/cream fungal material visible at stem base
- Stem split to show pale interior pith
- Plant collapsed with dead/wilted leaves
- Located at soil line with sandy soil

This is a **stem** at the soil line. Top candidates: **Southern_Blight** (white mycelium at stem base) and **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** (white cotton mycelium, black sclerotia in stem).

Let me view reference images one at a time across candidates.
I've viewed 7 references across 4 classes. I need 1 more view to complete the budget of 8, covering another new class.

**Analysis Summary:**

The test image shows a tomato plant uprooted from sandy soil with:
- Stem cut open longitudinally at/near soil line
- **White material coating the stem base exterior** (mycelium)
- Pale cream interior pith visible
- No visible black sclerotia inside stem
- Sandy soil surroundings, dead/wilted foliage

**Comparison results:**
- **Southern_Blight/root/Bugwood_18.jpg**: Closest visual match — same scene of plant pulled from sandy soil with white mycelium at stem base
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot/stem/Bugwood_4.jpg**: Shows large black sclerotia inside cut stem — NOT visible in test image
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot/stem/Bugwood_21.jpg**: White bleached stem with visible black sclerotia dots — test image lacks visible sclerotia
- **Alternaria, Bacterial_Wilt, Southern_Bacterial_Wilt**: Clearly don't match

The absence of black sclerotia inside the stem rules out Sclerotinia. The white external mycelium at the stem base in sandy soil strongly matches Southern Blight.
